errors.what: The regex that rewrote the `_units` call sites also rewrote the helper's own body, producing `return _units(TOK, USE_TOK, text)` — infinite recursion on first call. It compiled clean; caught only by an AST check asserting no helper calls itself.
Comparison bug: normalised the run directory on only one side of the smoke_readback_train diff, then deleted the pre-refactor worktree before running it down — producing a spurious 'still differs'.

The `default` arm died three times mid-training with no traceback and no report (last at step 38,500). User: 'something was not installed, I believe the datasets, and skipped it fully.' The `seeds` path had no corpus guard at all.

Claude's proposed pre-check command used GRID_DIR=runs/pre_check inside a git worktree — output resolved relative to the worktree and would be deleted by the same command's `git worktree remove --force`. A second version depended on $REPO surviving in the shell.

Inserting `from types import SimpleNamespace` replaced the first `import os` and hit a multi-import line, producing `from types import SimpleNamespace, math, random, glob, sys`. Commit 7de4daf was pushed unable to import at all; py_compile passed it.

The _report split's free-variable analysis walked assignment targets only and missed the six FUNCTIONS defined inside main() (_retok, _save_ckpt, _config_audit, encpos, encwin, report_holdout) plus CORP, SEG_LEN, VALC, VAL_FRAC, _time. Crashed on the user's GPU with NameError: _retok.

The context also subtracted every name _report writes; `assigns = [... for ... in assigns]` reads and writes the same name, making it local and unbound. Crashed on the user's GPU with UnboundLocalError: assigns. Fixing it took the context from 39 to 136 values.
`pkill -f "equiv.sh"` matched the bash executing the command, killing Claude's own shell (exit 144) and several background tasks at once.

equiv.sh decided a side 'reached the report' by grepping for `SIG_MODE=learned`, which is on LINE 8 of every log. A run that died at startup counted as complete, and a partial log counted as 'already done, reusing' — either path could produce a false IDENTICAL.

The vmax4k/vmax8k arms were run at commit 37ecb20, which predates their definition in c6f54e6. `_flags_for` hit its `*)` fallback and returned empty, so three runs of plain `base` were logged under three arm names.

data_pilot is not pinned and `_pilot_corpus` tops it up with --resume, so the corpus changed between runs on different days. Claude had told the user to expect base to reproduce 1.962; it returned 2.239 and nothing was reproduced or refuted.

Two report verdict lines contradicted the numbers printed beside them: 'FLAT: the second half bought nothing' printed alongside its own 2.04→1.97, and 'turned upward at the very end' printed six lines after 'NOT DIVERGING — judge this run on bits/byte'.
longrun.sh never set TOKENIZER_PATH, so every arm wrote its vocabulary to the same data/dyntok.json and each run overwrote the last — only vmax8k_3's vocabulary survived.
Mangled commit messages — backticks inside a heredoc without quoting caused command substitution ('/bin/bash: line 27: assigns: command not found'); amended and force-pushed.
Several local verification runs hit harness limits: 10-minute foreground timeout (exit 143), rc=124, and one 2-minute static-check timeout — verification results arrived late or not at all.
